title: WarmCache: Exploiting STT-RAM Cache for Low-Power Intermittent Systems
problem: Energy harvesting systems (EHS) suffer from compulsory cache misses after power failures because volatile SRAM caches lose all data across power outages, forcing cold-start cache rebuilding on each power restoration. Existing non-volatile cache designs impose high write energy and latency overhead.
motivation: Intermittent computing on energy-harvested devices is increasingly important for IoT/edge applications, but power-outage-induced compulsory misses impose prohibitive performance penalties with traditional caches.
method: WarmCache uses an STT-RAM cache with relaxed thermal stability (reduced retention time) tuned so cache contents survive typical power outage durations without requiring full non-volatile persistence. The compiler partitions the program into regions and performs region-level error correction: at each region boundary, updated cache lines are scrubbed and any multi-bit retention errors trigger re-execution of that region. A region formation technique via stitching (combining short regions) and splitting (dividing long regions) aligns region boundaries with the STT-RAM scrubbing interval.
key_novelty: Using relaxed-retention STT-RAM (not fully non-volatile) to preserve cache warmth across power outages, combined with compiler-driven region-level error correction to handle retention failures without write-back overhead.
contributions: Insight that STT-RAM retention time need only exceed power outage duration, not persist indefinitely, enabling reduced thermal stability and lower write energy.
Region-level error correction scheme: scrubbing at region boundaries and re-executing on detected multi-bit errors.
Compiler region formation with stitching and splitting to match region size to scrubbing interval.
1.3-1.4x average performance improvement over state-of-the-art EHS cache designs.
baselines: state-of-the-art STT-RAM cache design for EHS
limitations: Relies on power outage durations being shorter than the relaxed STT-RAM retention time; longer outages would cause data loss and correctness failures.
primary_theme: Relaxed-retention STT-RAM cache for intermittent energy-harvesting systems
